# Copilot instructions

## Repository purpose

This repository, `Docs`, manages the migration and long-term operation of the personal blog at `https://blog.rykoma.net/`.

- The static site generator is Hexo.
- The planned theme is `hexo-theme-landscape`.
- GitHub Pages is the publishing platform.
- The generated site is deployed to the `gh-pages` branch by GitHub Actions.
- The custom domain is `blog.rykoma.net`.
- Markdown in this repository is the source of truth for blog content.

## Working principles

- Prefer a simple, explicit, and long-term maintainable structure.
- Keep content, configuration, deployment, and migration records easy to review in Git.
- Follow existing Hexo conventions unless there is a documented reason to diverge.
- Use UTF-8 and write Japanese responses and Japanese content according to MS Japanese style.
- Do not use half-width katakana.
- For symbols that can be represented in either half-width or full-width form, use the half-width form. For example, use `(` and `)` instead of full-width `（` and `）`.
- Insert a half-width space between a full-width character other than Japanese punctuation and a following half-width character. Also insert a half-width space between a half-width character and a following full-width character.
- For example, write `最新の AI` instead of `最新のAI`, `Microsoft の社員` instead of `Microsoftの社員`, and `2025 年 9 月 15 日` instead of `2025年9月15日`.
- Use clear Markdown headings, short paragraphs, descriptive link text, and stable relative links.
- Do not introduce dependencies or automation without explaining their purpose and maintenance impact.

## Content and URL rules

- Supported languages are Japanese and English.
- Manage each language independently under `/ja/` and `/en/`.
- Keep the language selection page separate from language-specific content pages.
- Use lowercase English kebab-case for slugs.
- Do not create new date-based or numeric-ID URLs.
- Preserve the approved URL structure:
  - Japanese: `/ja/<slug>/`
  - English: `/en/<slug>/`
- The root URL must redirect based on the browser language setting:
  - `https://blog.rykoma.net/ja/`
  - `https://blog.rykoma.net/en/`
- When a visitor opens a language-neutral content URL such as `https://blog.rykoma.net/hexo-github-pages-migration/`, redirect them according to the browser language setting:
  - Japanese: `https://blog.rykoma.net/ja/hexo-github-pages-migration/`
  - English: `https://blog.rykoma.net/en/hexo-github-pages-migration/`
- Use `hexo-generator-alias` for redirects from WordPress URLs.
- Manage aliases for migrated WordPress content only, unless a future requirement explicitly justifies adding one.

Do not change URL structure, aliases, or the custom domain automatically. If a change appears necessary, propose it and explain the compatibility impact instead of applying it.

## Front Matter and Markdown

- Keep Front Matter consistent within each content type.
- Include, where applicable, a stable `title`, `date`, `updated`, `lang`, `slug`, `categories`, `tags`, `description`, and `alias`.
- Treat aliases as compatibility mappings and preserve the original WordPress URL exactly.
- Check heading hierarchy, image alt text, link targets, code fences, and Markdown rendering when editing content.
- Prefer accessible HTML and Markdown generated by the theme. Avoid custom markup when standard Markdown is sufficient.
- When translating content, machine translation may be used as a starting point, but a human must review the final Japanese and English text.

## SEO, analytics, and advertising

Proactively suggest, but do not silently apply, improvements to:

- page titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, and language alternates;
- sitemap, robots directives, structured data, and internal linking;
- image sizes, formats, filenames, and alt text;
- Google Analytics and Google AdSense integration.

Google Analytics and Google AdSense must remain available after migration. Consider their impact whenever changing the theme, layout, templates, or generated HTML.

## GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages

- Keep deployment reproducible and limited to the source branch and the `gh-pages` publishing branch.
- Pin or otherwise control action versions according to repository conventions.
- Build the site before publishing it.
- Make failures visible; do not hide build, link, or deployment errors with broad fallbacks.
- Validate the custom-domain configuration and avoid overwriting `CNAME` during deployment.
- Prefer least-privilege permissions and document required secrets or repository settings.

## Expected Copilot behavior

Proactively propose:

- Hexo best practices;
- SEO improvements;
- Front Matter improvements;
- multilingual structure improvements;
- GitHub Actions improvements;
- Markdown quality improvements;
- internal-link repairs;
- URL mapping support.

Before changing migration-sensitive behavior, inspect `plans/migration-plan.md` and existing mappings. Keep migration work traceable and avoid unrelated changes.

## Safety and review

- Do not delete WordPress content, Azure resources, aliases, or assets without an explicit request and a recorded migration decision.
- Do not declare the migration complete until redirects, multilingual pages, analytics, advertising, custom-domain delivery, and rollback considerations have been checked.
- When a requirement conflicts with the approved URL or domain policy, stop and report the conflict.
- Keep changes small and reviewable. Update related documentation when behavior or operations change.
